thread.title: Stocks Surge At Starting Bell; Boeing Lifts Dow Jones | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Surge At Starting Bell; Boeing Lifts Dow Jones | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks leapt into early gains Tuesday as Boeing ( BA ) led the Dow Jones industrials and earnings news bolstered early trade.
X Database giant Oracle ( ORCL ), Darden Restaurants ( DRI ) and truck maker Navistar ( NAV ) all jumped early on earnings news. Apple ( AAPL ) climbed and three of four FANG stocks leaned firmly higher. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) led the group though it still was smarting after its 4.5% drop on Monday. Freeport-McMoRan ( FCX ) and U.S. Steel ( X ) powered up as steelmakers and ore miners rallied for a second day.
The Dow Jones industrial average surged 1.3% in early trade. Boeing took an easy early lead among Dow Jones stocks after hiking its dividend and launching a new share-buyback initiative . Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) rebounded on comments made by the company's chief executive.
The S&P 500 leapt 1.1%. The Nasdaq Composite also swung 1.1% higher. Freeport-McMoRan, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Boeing dominated the lead among S&P 500 stocks. KLA-Tencor ( KLAC ), Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD jockeyed for the lead on the Nasdaq 100.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Fed Decision Looms; Housing Starts Surge The Federal Open Market Committee swings into its two-day meeting in Washington, with a policy decision due and news conference scheduled for Wednesday afternoon . Federal lawmakers were wrestling with the White House, attempting to reach a budget deal before a Friday night deadline.
Early economic news was positive, with the Commerce Department reporting November housing starts rose more than 3%, to an annualized rate of 1.256 million. Economists called for a decrease, to a pace of 1.221 million starts. Building permits surged 5%, to a rate of 1.328 million. Economists had projected a decrease here, as well, to an annualized rate of 1.255 million permits issued.
Dow Jones Eyes February Low; Small Caps In Bear Market Early advances have meant little in the recent market, which have consistently faded to late-day declines. The Dow Jones industrial average and the Nasdaq undercut their recent lows on Monday , shredding the effort to build a floor to the current consolidation. The Nasdaq's next test would come around the 6,630 level, which marks its low from February. The index has a cushion of almost 2% above that marker.
The Dow is a bit more than 1% above its April low, at 23,344. The S&P 500 also dived below its recent low marks, but also undercut its weak spots from April and February. It recovered to settle just above the 2,532 February low. The index has the potential to fashion a floor at this level.
Small caps ended Tuesday's session squarely in bear-market territory for the first time in two years. The Russell 2000 plummeted 2.3% Monday, leaving it 21% off its August high. The S&P Smallcap 600 also shed 2.3% Monday, ending 22% below its high from August. Indexes that drop more than 20% are considered to be technically in bear markets.
China Slides; Europe Mixed; Oil Prices Hit New Lows Stock markets dropped across Asia, tracing Monday's U.S. trade and after a speech from Chinese President Xi Jinping as Communist Party leaders and policymakers swung into their Central Economic Work Conference. The conference will set economic goals for 2019, and expectations are — among other things — for an easing of the national growth target to around 6.0% to 6.5%, vs. 2018's 6.5% target.
The Shanghai Composite dropped 0.8%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index dumped 1.1%. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 stumbled 1.8% but continued to hold support just above the 21,000 level.
In Europe, markets weakened in afternoon trade. Frankfurt's DAX trimmed its early gain to 0.3% higher near midday. The CAC-40 in Paris slipped 0.2% below its break-even line, and London's FTSE 100 dropped 0.4%.
Oil prices broke below a significant technical level, then trimmed early losses. West Texas Intermediate traded down 1.5% to just above $49 per barrel. WTI's first foray below the $49 level since September 2017 followed Monday's release of shale oil production estimates from the Energy Information Administration. WTI has been struggling to hold above the $50 level since Nov. 23. Europe's Brent crude benchmark fell 1.2% to just below $59. The American Petroleum Institute releases its weekly oil supply estimates this afternoon.
Dow Jones: Boeing Dividend, Apple Jobs Dow stock Boeing throttled up 4.7%, after a note from Canaccord called the company's dividend increase and share-buyback program bullish. The aerospace leader announced late Monday a 20% increase to its quarterly dividend , to $2.055 per share. The company also added $2 billion to its share-buyback plan, raising the program to $20 billion. Canaccord kept its hold rating on the stock, due to overall economic and trade concerns, the note said.
Also on the Dow, Apple advanced 1.1%, as the stock looked to form a bottom to the 30% pullback begun in early October. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan noted that the company plans to invest $1 billion in facilities in Austin, Texas, and planned new facilities in a half-dozen other U.S. cities that will create 20,000 new U.S. jobs by 2023. That would push Apple's U.S. workforce well over 100,000, and make it a leader in the effort to shift supply chains back to the U.S . Mohan kept the stock's neutral rating with a $220 price target.
Stocks: Oracle, Navistar Nail Earnings Gains Oracle grabbed an early 4% gain, after reporting fiscal second-quarter revenue and earnings above expectations . The database pioneer has struggled to transition to a cloud-based model, and shares are down 4% so far this year. The stock is in a double-bottom base, with a possible buy point at 51.65.
